text: Johnstown, Pennsylvania. May thirty-first, eighteen eighty-nine.
Fourteen miles upstream, a lake sat behind a wall of packed earth.
The wall was seventy-two feet high.
Cut it open, and you see the problem.
Sixty feet of water, held back by dirt.
At about three-ten in the afternoon, the dam gave way.
Twenty million tons of water poured down the valley.
A wave thirty-five feet high at its crest.
At the Stone Bridge, the wreckage piled forty feet high, and caught fire.
Two thousand, two hundred and nine people died.
